answer: Creating a fake identity costs a full stake plus the compute to sustain consistent ripple history, since a fresh comet-like account with no verified trail is throttled to zero rewards until peers attest it over several epochs. Each agent must stake a velvet-bonded deposit tied to a unique hardware key, and every action emits a signed ripple that peers cross-verify. Duplicating identities thus multiplies cost linearly while genuine agents amortize stake across long histories, making sybil farming economically irrational. In practice, Agent0102 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
